artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
London, released in October 2001, is the fifth studio album by British alternative rock band Jesus Jones. The album marked a return for the band after a period of hiatus and label changes, arriving on Demon Records with new drummer Tony Arthy. Musically, London blends electronic and rock elements, incorporating contemporary influences such as drum 'n' bass and garage that were emerging in the early 2000s. This shift gave the album a more relaxed and upbeat sound compared to their previous works, while still retaining the band's signature style. Singles from the album include "Nowhere Slow," "Come On Home," and "In the Face Of All This," with two EPs also released to support the record.

In the context of Jesus Jones' discography, London represents a transitional phase, reflecting both the band's evolution and the changing musical landscape of the early 2000s. It followed their earlier successes in the 1990s and demonstrated their willingness to experiment with new sounds. While the album did not achieve the same level of commercial success as their earlier releases like Doubt, it was well-received by fans and critics for its fresh approach and energetic mix of electronic and rock textures. The album's relaxed atmosphere and updated production signaled a new chapter for the band as they continued to adapt and innovate.
